installationAndStart.summary: Reviewed the two-route preparation section before Lesson 1. Separate accessible tabs select starting from scratch or using an existing codebase; each contains its own installation/preflight prompt, project request and preparation steps in a bounded scroll area. Tab controls and the Lesson 1 link remain outside the scroll area. Direct links select the right guide; keyboard navigation, reduced-motion settings and JavaScript-free access are preserved. Both routes keep chat-first setup, Python/Node/npx checks, platform help and real user authorization for system installation. Homepage installation copy and its downloadable instructions remain synchronized; existing scope/history and final acceptance stay intact. Each lesson now has a Pocket Board prompt and an illustrative reply. All six prompt copy targets were checked in the browser at desktop and phone widths, and the prompt text is visible without JavaScript.

deliveryModes.summary: Homepage and School consistently default new work to Ship, reserve Loop for actual feedback on useful increments, and separate delivery style from Strict/Auto and cost depth. School explicitly chooses Ship/Auto and grants bounded plan approval only after confirming scope/resources. This is an explicit example mandate, not an unselected default or invented acceptance. Existing frozen deliveries retain their original policy. Release 4.8.10 makes the usable artifact available during Ship; optional early feedback adds no approval, routine stop or implied acceptance.

orchestration.summary: Receiving-agent coordination and explicit session-bound handoff remain accurate. The homepage and School now explain approval-bound per-child model/reasoning choices without transferring coordination. Exact plan pairs and cumulative allowances authorize later choices; profile candidates alone do not. Supported native starts/preflight retain the actual child and rationale; the current bound-thread UI bridge cannot dispatch pooled children. Independent expectations before material plan freeze and early functioning-core scrutiny supplement final integrated review. Historical relocation and attempt rules remain unchanged; declarations authenticate neither host identity nor arbitrary host calls. Release 4.8.10 continues the same review from the usable core to final readiness and changes default review prompts to reuse current evidence and assess relevant deltas; graph authority and dependencies are unchanged.

delegatedDecisions.summary: Homepage escalation and School delegation preserve explicit scope, resources and owner acceptance boundaries. The linked Story contract now permits only an actual present human to cancel or replace approved unaccepted work through a scoped typed decision. Existing approve/accept/orchestrate delegation and Auto cannot authorize this changed commitment. Each replacement is a separately unapproved plan; no past gate or final acceptance is invented. Cancelled/replaced corrections remain provenance targets but no longer contribute outgoing current proof/readiness obligations; a new active correction retains normal checks. The Pocket Board conversation requires agreement on scope and resources before implementation and explicitly reserves changes to those limits, publication and acceptance for the human.

resourceUse.summary: Planning, authoring, review, corrections and integration still belong to the cumulative mandate. Approved pool starts include failure/retry/rework/reviewer history; optional finite-decimal cost reservations retain original estimates and maximum known charges. Running observations can block later starts. Neither unknown usage nor lower reports refund resources. Host-hidden model/effort/cost remains unknown, and reservations are not provider billing caps. School elapsed-time examples still require available host measurement and actual owner authority to raise limits. No universal cost-saving measurement is claimed.

verificationAndAcceptance.summary: AIM 4.8.12 retains restraint in new automated tests, reuse of meaningful evidence and zero-new-test delivery when sufficient. This release clarifies that reduced test volume does not reduce scrutiny of original outcomes. Reviewer/TDO, default Native review assignments and the Copilot adapter classify findings by consequence; advisory labels or green checks cannot waive material defects or missing decisive evidence. The adapter no longer marks a delivery ready merely by listing remaining manual checks. Independent bounded scenarios produced correction for a missing required CSV column, readiness with zero new tests for covered help text, and a targeted restore observation for missing core evidence without assuming a product defect. Homepage and Lesson 6 agree; unchanged startup prompts, layout, interaction and learning observations are reused. No new gate, report, exhaustive journey or test quota is introduced. This supports instruction coherence, not a measured future quality gain.

modelsAndEvidence.summary: Homepage retains the dated 18 October 2026 AIM assessment (96.5/100), 30 September baseline (49.8), differing conditions, unfinished Native delivery and absence of a fresh paired or general quality/cost claim. AIM 4.8.12 inherits no new Enigma score. Dated 4.7.5 screenshots remain historical. School keeps its optional model setup as a suggestion, then explains exact approved pairs, task/risk/budget judgment and separate review. The revised conversation proposes a pool before approval, then distinguishes requested settings from reported/unknown settings. Actual host/account controls remain binding; a prompt cannot create capability. Three short native probes establish explicit requests and returned responses only; unavailable telemetry and relative model performance are not inferred.
